scope.note: the 3D problems of polyhedrainpolyhedra.wiki (Platonic, Archimedean, Catalan, prisms, antiprisms, elongated prisms) with 2 to 100 pieces; 4D-6D are not included; then PolyPack's own problems in the same scheme (prisms and antiprisms with 7, 9, 10 and 11 sides in themselves and in a cube, and their prisms of height 1.5, 2 and 3 in a cube; bipyramids and trapezohedra, the canonical duals of the prisms and antiprisms, in themselves and in a cube), whose records are PolyPack research only

conventions.problem_id:
polyhedra//

: P copies of the piece solid in s times the container solid; code is upstream's in (e.g. cubintet)
conventions.solids: canonical solids of python/polyhedra/solids_exact.json (upstream src/solids_exact.json), centred at the origin; unit edges except Catalan solids (polar reciprocals of the unit-edge Archimedean solids about the midsphere) and elongated prisms (lateral edges 1.5, 2, 3)
conventions.pose: [x, y, z, qw, qx, qy, qz]: the canonical piece rotated by q / |q| (rotation H(q) / |q|^2) and centred at (x, y, z); the container s C is centred at the origin in its canonical orientation
conventions.score: s (score_cert = config.s, proven valid by python/polyhedra/certify.py); smaller is better
conventions.score_float: the float container scale of the stored poses at the same centres (pieces keep their clearance); s_tight, where given, is upstream's uncertified touching limit
conventions.clearance: records from the wiki keep its convention: every pair and wall at least 1e-7 apart (some wall gaps were cut to about 1e-10 by certified wall-padding refinements)
conventions.display: score_cert rounded to the nearest at 6 decimals from its exact binary64 value
conventions.bound: kind volume: [EST] n vol(piece) <= s^3 vol(container), so s >= (n vol(piece) / vol(container))^(1/3)
conventions.origin: the file the configuration comes from: upstream's records/... at commit cbf76f2f (sources.wiki.files) or a PolyPack research file (sources.polypack); for a PolyPack search, start is the packing it started from (none for a start from random positions) and, for a search of the compute study, runs are its runs from that start, as its run logs show them
conventions.wiki: the wiki's record of the case (its smallest certified s_full in the repository) and its page; file is given when the configuration here comes from elsewhere
conventions.literature: published values without coordinates (value, source, url, printed precision)
conventions.configs: the configurations are kept apart, one file per problem: configs/<code>.jsonl has one line per P, in increasing P, each {"P", "config": {s, pieces}}; config_at = [offset, length] gives the byte offset and length of the record's line (without its newline), so that a reader can read that one configuration alone
conventions.polypack: records of PolyPack's own problems (no wiki record): origin.file is the PolyPack research file, origin.start the construction the configuration's lineage starts from (none for a search from random positions), origin.runs the searches and subset steps after it and origin.seed the last step's seed, in short; method states the whole lineage in full

credit.platonic: soft-to-rigid method by Yohei Nakajima (2026); generalization to Platonic solids, basin-hopping search and exact certification developed with Claude (Anthropic) under Alejandro Zarzuelo's direction
credit.families: soft-to-rigid method by Yohei Nakajima (2026); generalization to Archimedean, Catalan, prism and antiprism solids, basin-hopping search and certification developed with Claude (Anthropic) under Alejandro Zarzuelo's direction

method.platonic: soft-to-rigid homotopy (inscribed balls hardened into the solid under inward pressure), then SLSQP tightening with per-pair separating planes
method.families: generalized soft-to-rigid homotopy (r-rounding of the solid hardened under inward pressure), basin hopping, then sequential-LP / SLSQP tightening with per-pair separating planes

records.method:
This batch contains 23 fresh campaign cases, distinct from all 54 earlier fresh archives: 19 antiprism cases, three prism cases and one pentakis-dodecahedron self-packing. Sixteen improve the pinned current nominal/reference bound; seven improve complete native certificates without claiming a new ideal nominal value.

The main new construction places fixed-phase antiprism rings and whole axial slots inside actual complete regular-prism parents. The forced phase comes from the full cyclic difference grid. Every child, sibling slab and inherited parent separator is retained. Literal whole-owner prefixes give additional complete cases. For six hexagonal antiprisms in a cube, one common center contraction releases the artificial parent facets while all 15 target-pair separators remain simultaneously valid; the certified side is 2.862714781480716. No angle sweep is used.

A reciprocal golden-host inclusion and common return give eleven pentakis dodecahedra in their own host at 2.82404531854329. The three prism cases retain complete source-column and height/collar operations from the reviewed bank.

All active witnesses passed independent source, full geometry and current-public/private comparisons, followed by both official checks on the packaged native files. The archive preserves complete parent packings, physical decoders, common-return certificates and original source attribution. Some provenance audit scripts require the authenticated upstream Git snapshot or reviewed-source registry; the bundled official native validators are directly replayable.

Credit the new finite constructions exactly to PingYou Ltd. Original donors and their authors remain explicitly credited. These contributions may be published under the repository’s MIT license. No global optimality is claimed. Fresh campaign cases, live site credit and submission acceptance are tracked separately.
